key_insight: A coupled CEL simulation and ANN surrogate can accurately predict friction stir welding quality in HDPE, revealing that bottom-surface preheating stabilizes force and temperature and improves weldability.
engineering_relevance: This work provides a practical process-optimization route for thermoplastic welding by linking physics-based modeling with fast machine-learning predictions to identify defect-free operating windows.
method: 3D coupled Eulerian-Lagrangian (CEL) model of HDPE FSW under varied rotation speed, travel speed, and bottom preheating
Two multilayer perceptron ANNs trained on experimental time-series data for temperature and axial force prediction
Combined simulation-experiment process mapping to locate defective vs defect-free welding conditions
evidence_signal: The ANN models achieved strong agreement with experiments with R² values from 0.91 to 0.99, and the CEL model matched observed void formation and thermal/mechanical responses.
watch_item: The process map is based on a specific HDPE setup and tested parameter range, so broader transfer to other polymers, tool geometries, or thicknesses should be validated before deployment.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
